reason: Mechanism real at HEAD 2e23b46: buildWireSources (internal/taint/redaction/source.go:110-111) passes source.Name verbatim into model.NewSourceRedactedString, so a source classified sensitive by its name serializes that unredacted name on the wire. Reproduced independently through the public taint API plus the production MessagePack encoder, and on a full woven orchestrion build (Go 1.26.6) with a real HTTP request whose credential-shaped query key reached database/sql sinks: the captured span event shows name=token:abcdefghijklm with redacted=true while the value was pattern-replaced. Default configuration, no env overrides. Severity downgraded from Critical to Medium: the only data reachable through this path is client-controlled key/name structure (an attacker exfiltrating their own credential-shaped key), never user or server secrets, which live in source values and are redacted; and keeping source names is the deliberate uniform cross-language IAST design (dd-trace-java SourceAdapter.java:75-80, dd-trace-js vulnerable-formatter, dd-trace-python reporter.py:361-363 all keep the name and redact only the value). It remains a genuine narrow bypass of the redaction contract (credential-shaped string leaves with redacted:true) that should be fixed. Not a documented README limitation. Shares one root cause with sink-redaction-source-F1: the same buildWireSources/NewSourceRedactedString call site deciding what a redacted wire source retains (F1: content-derived pattern; F2: unredacted name); F3 is unrelated.
